newsitem.title: USA: U.S. light foreign crudes tight, demand buoyant.
newsitem.headline: U.S. light foreign crudes tight, demand buoyant.

text.p: U.S. refiners bought several cargoes of light, sweet foreign crudes this week, but paucity of supplies continued to fuel light crude demand Thursday.
The tendency to secure barrels drove prices for domestic alternatives higher, with trades heard fixed as far forward as December, in anticipation of an unworkable arbitrage.
"Several refiners picked up Brent and Cusiana, but buying came into the market instead of selling," one Midwest trader said, noting a rally in Louisiana light and heavy grades.
At least three Cusianas for first-half/mid Nov traded this week at Dec WTI plus 10 cents fob.
Colombia's Ecopetrol Thursday offered a Nov 21-25 cargo into the market, sourcing for bids, traders said.
Brent was thinly discussed with one European trader who sold three parcels earlier this week, again rumored to have sold another two parcels to U.S. refiners today.
But some maintained the trader had swapped out a ULCC on subjects for a VLCC, and was not likely to have moved more Brent to the U.S. Gulf.
Brent this week traded at Dec WTI plus 50-55 cents cif.
Elsewhere in the region, YPF offered Canadon Seco for Nov 28-29 at WTI minus $1.95 fob, including lightering costs.
Vasconia reported awarded earlier this week out of a Colombian tender was heard transacted twice around WTI minus $2.12 fob, but this could not be immediately confirmed.
In the U.S. after market, a full cargo and a partial were reported traded for Dec Brent at $24.28 a barrel, above London's IPE close at $24.15 a barrel.
Intermonth Brent spreads were mostly unchanged with Nov/Dec at 46/49 cents, and Dec/Jan at 66/69 cents.
Earlier, Brent/Dubai for Feb traded at $2.16 a barrel, and Dubai intermonth spreads for Feb/Mar at 54 cents, and Mar/Apr at 53 cents.
